fact: Raskolnikov murders the pawnbroker Alyona Ivanovna and, when she returns unexpectedly, her half-sister Lizaveta, both with an axe.
evidence: the axe murder in Part I

fact: The morning after the murder, Raskolnikov receives a summons to appear at the district police superintendent's office at half-past nine.
evidence: "an ordinary summons from the district police-station to appear that day at half-past nine"

fact: Marmeladov, a drunken former civil servant, tells Raskolnikov in a tavern that his daughter Sonya has been forced into prostitution to feed the family.
evidence: Marmeladov's tavern confession in Part I

fact: Marmeladov is fatally trampled by a carriage in the street; Raskolnikov gives his last money to the family to pay for the funeral.
evidence: Marmeladov's death and Raskolnikov's donation in Part II

fact: Raskolnikov's mother Pulcheria Alexandrovna writes describing Dunya's engagement to Luzhin and her earlier ordeal with Svidrigailov, her former employer.
evidence: the mother's letter in Part I

fact: Svidrigailov tells Raskolnikov that the ghost of his dead wife, Marfa Petrovna, has visited him three times since her burial.
evidence: "Marfa Petrovna is pleased to visit me... She has been three times."

fact: The examining magistrate Porfiry Petrovich conducts a psychological cat-and-mouse interrogation of Raskolnikov, implying suspicion without ever directly accusing him.
evidence: the Porfiry interrogation scenes, Part III

fact: Luzhin secretly plants a 100-rouble note in Sonya's pocket at the Marmeladov memorial dinner, then publicly accuses her of theft, as revenge on Raskolnikov for turning the family against him.
evidence: "a folded 100-rouble note does indeed fly out of one of the pockets"

fact: Svidrigailov reveals that he overheard Raskolnikov's confession to Sonya through the wall of the adjoining room, since he has been renting the room next door.
evidence: "has been residing next door to Sonya"

fact: Svidrigailov offers Dunya 10,000 roubles to break off her engagement to Luzhin; enraged, she refuses and orders him out.
evidence: "offer her 10,000 roubles to break it off... Dunya, enraged, tells him to get out"

fact: Svidrigailov gives Sonya 3,000 roubles before his death, funding her eventual journey to Siberia with Raskolnikov.
Svidrigailov commits suicide by shooting himself, after a night of disturbing dreams, in a public place shortly before dawn.
Raskolnikov confesses to the murders at the police station after first going to Sonya and kissing the ground at the Hay Market crossroads, per her earlier instruction.
Raskolnikov is sentenced to eight years of penal servitude in Siberia; Sonya follows him there.
evidence: the Epilogue's sentencing and Sonya's move to Siberia

fact: In the Epilogue, Raskolnikov has a fever dream about a plague of self-righteous ideological "trichinae" that turns people against each other, shortly before his spiritual turn toward Sonya and the Gospels.
evidence: the Epilogue's dream of the trichinae/plague
